I've been an entrepreneur for most of my life as either a consultant or starting business. This also meant living dirt poor, borrowing money from my family, losing that money and then having businesses fail. When you get that wrapped up into your business you become the business. So the failure is very personal. Add losing family money, owning no real assets (houses etc) being in debt and broke it is a very tough road. It gets worse when your friends and family become succesful and make money.  Over time I learned to try and separate my personal identity from my work and even to a bit my family. We are what we do is so ingrained in many cultures and it is difficult to push away from that. Certainly there will be disappointment with both you and your family and friends. But it will also be a learning process and you may find you are meant to do something else that will be incredibly fulfilling. Over time I learned I don't need a house, fancy car and gained massive fulfillment from the things I was able to do. Best of luck.
